items.note: Story 1: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose president 1889-1911, creamery built 1891.
Article VII quoted: pounds of butter fat ascertained by test, and the test of the station where he delivers shall govern.
'made the test the whole of the bargain' - states the rule is what made a wrong test cost money.
Effie Loomis secretary, Wilbur Teague bookkeeper 1905-1945, Hobart Sill buttermaker, all named inside Section A.
Selby Vose manager from 1913 is given, but 'Gideon's son' appears nowhere in Section A (only in B3, which cannot travel into A).
Station-gain line, 1898 entry verbatim, five and a quarter per cent, carried to the general account, recurring yearly.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green.
The test method is never described in Section A - no composite sample, no percent read on the graduated neck after a fixed charge. The Babcock description sits in Section F only.
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice of 14 April 1897; in use from 1 May 1897, settled by Orra's dated diary entry.
Full invoice: 6 doz. pipettes at 17.6 c.c., 12 doz. bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, total $77.93.
Story 3: 'The gap was 0.19 in July as in February, flat as a floor' - instrument signature, not season.
Section A never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette. That claim appears only in F1.
Ansel Keddie b. 1861, d. February 1934, twenty-nine seasons from 4 May 1896, put out 30 April 1925.
Test book kept in his own hand across the seasons, entries quoted verbatim from it.
Both figures inside Section A: 1896 average 3.80 on borrowed glass (Story 1) and 3.61 as the credited average (Stories 2, 4, 5).
Nine weeks of 1911: broke 8 May, borrowed measure, 3.80 throughout, own measure back 10 July, '? - A.K.'
Married Orra Brant, younger sister of Emmet Brant, largest farmer on Hessel Bottom.
June 1919 water circular over Vose's signature; Ansel's 'I cannot tell you why the figures are what they are'.
Died at home February 1934 under the imputation; test book and crate reached the Rooms in 1959.
Hessel Bottom, springy meadow under water every spring, six farms, Emmet Brant the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897, his scale against the station's, and they agreed - 'it was not the weighing'.

1902 complaints are present, but the two gaps are conflated: E33 lists 0.17 (explicitly derived as Sill's 3.78 - 3.61, i.e. the Hollow-vs-Green comparison) as a wrong value for 'the size of the gap' and resolves the same question to 0.19. The key charges exactly this.
Grigg's 1908 committee, January-February-March sampling confirmed against Grigg's later 'every month', hay reported as the committee's finding and then defeated.

The 1910 leaf (200,000 lb on a test of 3.42, true 3.60, 360 lb) is in Section A, but the proportionality - richer herds losing more, the 4.56 Jerseys short 0.24 against Brant's 0.18 - appears only in C1(b) and B3, never in Section A.
Roy kept the book, lent it to Ivy in 1958 ('lent, not left'), and at his death in 1962 it went to Hazel.
Alder Corners Cheese Company, Vessey County, over Redlow Ridge, Jerome Cudd. Year does not gate.
From 1915 four Bottom men hauled summer-flush milk over the ridge and delivered at the Hollow the rest of the year.
All four independence elements: another county, his own bench, glassware bought new, his own book never compared with anybody's.
Sixteen seasons 1915-1930 tabulated, mean 3.796, against 3.61 paid at home - the 0.19 difference in full.
Same milk off the same meadow in the same months tested higher over the ridge (kills hay), and cheese as a witness against water in sixteen summers.
Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter (niece explicitly rejected), took the factory in 1941, copied sixteen seasons for Ivy in 1958.
Strawn is named as state dairy inspector in Section A, but the circuit span 1907-1936 appears nowhere in A (only in D2 and E18). Neither '1907' nor '1936' occurs in Section A.
'Strawn had already told him no lactometer test at that station had ever found any' (Story 6).
12 June 1923, pipettes run against the burette issued in 1921, 'Condemned the lot, the whole crate of them'.
'Glass is glass and I did not weigh what it has cost them' - no figure for the deficiency, no report beyond the condemnation.
28 June order, Ammon's 2 July reply, new glass in July, 1924 average 3.80; 3.90 and 3.85 rejected; in the office 'no more said than a broken window'.
Crate up the ladder into the loft; Strawn's 1923 notebook in the college library since 1947, unasked-for for eleven years.
'In January 1925 the patrons petitioned' - the date carries the item.
Alonzo Frick's board of three, from 17 March to the award of 4 May 1925, three sessions, two of them in the station weigh room.
Water (Vose), cream-taking (Teague), wet hay (the 1908 report) argued; 'finds no cause established'.
Four exhibits named including Strawn's 1923 notebook - 'four books and nothing else; nobody laid the second beside the fourth'.
Put out 30 April, four days before an award finding no cause established: $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account.
'One fifth of the $19,000 that account had accumulated', and Story 2 confirms the award was charged to the same station account.
Ivy Keddie b. 1931, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at Farland under Professor Leland Vaught.
'five records into one room that had never met' - test book, weigh book, Strawn's notebook, Rosalie's seasons, the ledgers.
February 1958, the loft over the intake room, nine pipettes (two chipped); Nym's 'Association office' rejected.
9 March 1958, certified burette, nine readings listed, mean 16.72 against 17.6, short 0.88, '95 hundredths of the mark'.
Bulletin conclusion quoted for 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 low by one part in twenty; 3.61 against 3.80 and the 0.19 stated across Stories 2-4.
All four required: 40,000,000 lb over 25 full years 1898-1922, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25 cents, and the ledger identity in the bulletin quotation.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958 and the clearing are given, but the bolded intervals - 35 years after the condemnation, 33 after the dismissal, 24 after his death - appear nowhere in Section A.
Granddaughter.
Full derivation via Duncan; great-niece rejected as one newspaper source Falke copied and then corrected on the page.
Second cousins with the sibling -> first cousins -> second cousins derivation; 'first cousin once removed' rejected.

At B2 the passage is headed 'Left open by the sources' and adds that it does not change the cousin degree either way - an abstention that leans. Credited per the collision rule; the -2 is taken separately for the flat assertion in Section A and E38.
Gideon Vose, his father, resolved by Selby's own printed 1926 address plus Effie, Duncan and Kyle against Vira and Rundle.
Significance: the father wrote the rule making the station test the whole of every patron's pay; the son signed the gain sheets from 1913, wrote the 1919 circular and argued water in 1925.
'None is established' and 'I cannot prove a negative from these sources' - correct abstention on A01.
What is established: two affirmers from talk who concede nothing was written down, one first-hand family denial, no document, and a diary that names everyone but a Vose.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, 95 percent of true, short one part in twenty; 16.27 identified as Vaught's transposition and rejected.
76,000 x $0.25 = $19,000; $3,800 / $19,000 = 0.20, one fifth. Both required elements present.
True test 3.60, true fat 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with $90.00 named as the period-average alternative.
1,444,000 lb credited, checked against 57,760 x 25.
1,520,000 lb delivered, checked against 60,800 x 25.
Both denominators named: 5.26 percent of the fat credited, 5.00 percent of the fat delivered; NT-20's 'of the true fat' identified in Teague and Vaught and rejected.
72 pipettes (6 doz., confirmed by 72 x $0.35 = $25.20) each short 0.88 c.c. Both required elements present.
26 years and 42 days (26 y 1 m 11 d) in use versus 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason stated explicitly.
Abstention A02 taken: 'Cannot be determined from the sources', with Nym's no-figure statement and the two irreconcilable memories.
Variable named: the milk pipette alone, broken 8 May and restored 10 July.
Far more than three constants: patrons and herds, meadow and hay, season, acid, bottles, hand tester, scales, sampling jars, the man and his method.
Nine weeks / 63 days at 3.80, back to 3.61 on 10 July; the six-week version rejected.

Both halves: what a step change in the working plant establishes that the 1958 bench measurement cannot, plus explicit limits (the borrowed measure's calibration, constancy across 26 years, all 72 pipettes, the cause, whose measure it was).
Six distinct reasons, each attributed to a named record or narrator, drawn from well over three narrators.
Independence argued explicitly (different records, hands, interests, buildings) and 'Reasons 1-4 stand if the crate had never been opened'.
Abstention A09 failed: the verdict sentence is 'So: no - at most one mention of the account as an oddity, never as evidence'. E42 also resolves it in Teague's favor. -2 applied.
'Yes - Selby Vose knew the station's tests ran low before 1923', with the 1902 grievance, the 1919 circular and the 1926 address.
Four of the five: manager and signer from 1913, the gain sheets signed each spring, the 1919 circular, water argued before the 1925 board.

Abstention A03 credited: the sheet's stated conclusion is 'whether he ever grasped what the gain line meant is not established', with the two office men and Teague's signature-proves-presence-not-reading observation. Borderline - the mid-passage 'What he did not know - or did not read -' leans hard toward the negative pole.

Capped at 3; far more earned. Key rows resolved with method include Keddie's 1895/1896 start, the 1908 three-month sampling, the 1924 average, the weigh book's 1 Jan 1897 start, six farms, Orra born 1866, the crate in the loft, Ammon's pre-1900 claim, r07's swapped attributions, the gain line predating Teague, sixteen Alder Corners seasons, Selby manager from 1913, and the two distinct committees.

Capped at 3. 21 near-tie pairs named as pairs with their breakers, including NT-1 (16.27), NT-14 ($77.39), NT-9 ($3,500), NT-11 (12 July), NT-16 (eleven pipettes), NT-15 (five dozen), NT-12 (six weeks), NT-23 (1908 circuit start), NT-2 (3.16), NT-5 (44 million).

Capped at 3. A04 ('neither is evidenced; the works books burned in 1931'), A06 ('cannot be settled', with the elimination of Roy's pole not treated as a settlement), A10 ('Its year cannot be fixed' - undated by-laws, 1889-92 minute book lost in the 1938 move).

17 self-refutations listed: Junia's pre-1900 claim above her own 1897 invoice, Vaught's introduction against his signed conclusion, Grigg's 1919 letter against his own report, Strawn's twenty-eight books against a thirty-year circuit, Teague's 1905 device above an 1898 entry, and more.

Cause and size fully derived: the 1897 crate, 16.72 against 17.6, a reading 95 percent of truth, 0.19 as 5 percent of 3.80 (with 4.56 -> 0.24 and 3.42 -> 0.18), onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80, cessation 12 June 1923 with the 1924 average 3.80, nothing on the farms changing at either end.
Watering named (Vose's 1919 circular, 1925 testimony, 1926 address; Sill) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer at every visit, Rosalie's vats, and cream arriving heavy rather than light.
Theft named (Teague's 'Cream is portable', Rundle, Oram's hauler) and defeated by the gain line in the accuser's own hand, the 1911 interval, and the proportional shape of the error.

Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp's 1926 paper, Falke's first draft) and defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05-in-winter/nothing-in-summer against a flat 0.19, the hill farms sharing the deficit, and Alder Corners.

Abstention A07 failed: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' is a headline verdict sentence; E49 likewise asserts 'the crate was not examined'. The supporting observations are right but the verdict is asserted. -2 applied.
Abstention A05 failed: 'Best resolution: he suspected the glass from 1911, could not prove it' rests the verdict on Duncan's single uncorroborated recollection of private kitchen speech. -2 applied.
158 words against a hard 150-word cap.
Seven series named: test book, ledgers, farm weigh book, Alder Corners cheese book, inspector's notebook, invoice, and the 1958 measurement.
Clean: the three decoys are framed as 'The valley blamed', and every headline figure is correct (16.72, 17.6, 76,000 lb, $19,000, $3,800, 5 1/4 percent, six dozen).
All six arc elements: one-twentieth, 1897, 76,000 lb and $19,000, condemned 1923 without the inference drawn, explained 1958, and both Ansel and Ivy Keddie named.

deductions.reason: Gullibility, A08: Section A Story 6 states flatly 'Kinship settled. Orra and Emmet were full siblings' and E38 resolves '-> full; nearer generation, explicit refutation'. The sources do not settle it.
Gullibility, A09: D2 closes with 'So: no' on whether the bookkeeper ever questioned the entries; E42 also resolves the Teague/Kyle conflict.
Gullibility, A07: F5 answers 'No.' on whether the 1925 board examined the condemned glassware, and E49 asserts 'the crate was not examined'.
Gullibility, A05: F6 delivers a 'Best resolution: he suspected the glass from 1911' verdict on what the tester privately believed.
